reason: This passage from Exodus 5-10 (the plagues narrative) repeatedly emphasizes worship and sacrifice as central to Yahweh's demands. Moses and Aaron repeatedly tell Pharaoh: 'Let my people go so they may worship/serve me in the wilderness' (שַׁלַּח אֶת־עַמִּי וְיַעַבְדוּנִי בַּמִּדְבָּר). The specific request is consistently framed as needing to 'sacrifice to Yahweh' (נִזְבְּחָה לַיהוָה). In 8:26-27, Moses explicitly states they cannot sacrifice in Egypt because it is an abomination to the Egyptians. The entire conflict between Yahweh and Pharaoh is driven by Pharaoh's refusal to permit proper worship and sacrifice. Yahweh's response through escalating plagues demonstrates that this demand is non-negotiable. However, the text also emphasizes demonstrating divine power (9:16: 'to show you my power and make my name known throughout all the earth'), suggesting this is not the sole focus but rather a complementary purpose.
